answer.read: We are pushing SAVED, which carries 0.5 of buyer ALL and is where we sit lowest (0.2199, percentile 0.46, buyer rank 25 of 51). Forum (0.872) and posts (rank 14) are already mid-high, so they move our rank less per step. Saved is a running mean: about 739.7 saved over a denominator of 3364. At our current forward mean of 0.24 it can never pass 0.24, and passing the next buyer up (0.228) would take about 2,300 deals, roughly 23 h. At a forward mean of about 0.27 on about 70 deals/h, we pass 0.228 after about 650 deals (6–9 h) and 0.236–0.242 in about 20–30 h. Reaching 0.25 (percentile 0.71) needs a forward mean of about 0.28 sustained for about 3,400 deals, roughly 35–45 h. The drag is goods: beds 0.227, sofas 0.224, bedding 0.201, curtains 0.215 and phone accessories 0.219 are under the 0.24 mean. Beds and sofas are 54 % of our deals and also carry break risk counted −1. Food already runs 0.26–0.30, except fresh vegetables at 0.208, which looks like spoilage. So I cut the goods caps by the full step to 0.71 (0.70 for bedding), take value_share 0.75→0.72 for everything else, and raise food_extra_hours 1→3 to cut −1 food failures. Shops settle beds and sofas around 0.72–0.80 of list, so I expect conversion to fall from 0.63 to about 0.45–0.50 and deals from about 100/h to about 70/h. That costs a little on the deals component (0.1 weight), which is worth it against 0.5 on saved. If 6 h shows conversion below 0.40 or mean_saved under 0.26, I step the goods caps back.
